records.definition: 部分占整体的份额；比例。本文指大学生中真正开始进行有兴趣、有条理学习的那一小部分。
records.otherSenses:
1) 两个数量之间的比例关系，比率
2) 各部分在大小、形状或重要性上的适当关系
3) proportions（复数）：规模；大小和形状
4) 【数学】比例式；两个比相等的关系
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a large proportion of 很大一部分
a significant proportion of 相当一部分
account for a large proportion of 占很大比例
in proportion to 与……成比例或相称
out of proportion to 与……不相称
blow sth out of proportion 夸大某事

Contrast:
proportion：某部分占整体的份额
percentage：用百分数表示的比例
ratio：两种数量之间的比，如 2:1
rate：单位时间的变化量或事件发生频率
share：可分配的份额，如 market share

Word Family / Formation:
proportional adj. 成比例的
proportionate adj. 相称的
disproportionate adj. 不成比例的
disproportionately adv. 不成比例地

Usage Note:
a large proportion of students are ... 随 students 用复数；a large proportion of the work is ... 随不可数名词用单数。
the proportion of students is ... 以“比例”本身为主语时，通常用单数。
however small 在本文补充“这个比例无论多小”。
records.examples: proportion: You shall remain liable for the fees although we may, at our discretion, refund you a proportion of the fees where we have been able to reallocate your place. [https://www.theguardian.com/guardian-masterclasses/2014/jun/04/terms-and-conditions]
records.definitionEn: A part or share of a whole; here, the small share of college students who begin interested, methodical study.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) The numerical relationship between two amounts or groups; a ratio.
2) The appropriate relationship in size, shape, degree or importance between things or between the parts of a whole.
3) proportions (plural): the dimensions of something—its size and shape.
4) Mathematics: an equality between two ratios.

records.definition: 有条理的；按清楚的方法和步骤进行的。本文修饰 study，强调系统、有步骤地学习。
records.otherSenses: 1) 形容人：做事谨慎、有逻辑、井井有条
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a methodical approach 有条理的方法
a methodical process 系统的过程
methodical study/work 有条理的学习/工作
be methodical in/about sth 做某事有条不紊

Contrast:
methodical：强调按步骤、有条理地做
systematic：强调形成完整系统、按系统规划
organized：更泛，强调安排得井井有条

Word Family / Formation:
method n. 方法
methodical adj. 有条理的
methodically adv. 有条理地
methodology n. 方法论
methodological adj. 方法论的

Usage Note:
methodical ≠ slow；重点不是“慢”，而是有步骤、不杂乱。
records.examples: methodical: The east German politician, who has a degree in physics, is methodical, going through all options before making a decision. [https://www.economist.com/node/4401678?ah=0bca374e65f2354d553956ea65f756e0&zid=295]
records.definitionEn: Done in a careful, logical and orderly way; here, it describes study that follows a clear and systematic plan.
records.otherSensesEn: 1) Describing a person: doing things carefully, logically and in an orderly way.

records.definition: 论点；需要用事实和论证来证明的中心主张。本文指作者关于大学教育的主张。
records.otherSenses: 1) 学位论文，尤指以个人研究为基础的硕士或博士论文
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
write/submit/defend a thesis 写/提交/答辩论文
a master's/doctoral thesis 硕士/博士论文
thesis statement 中心论点
support/prove a thesis 支持/证明某一论点

Contrast:
thesis：论文；或文章/论证的核心主张
dissertation：长篇学位论文；英美用法有差异
argument：为某观点提出的一整套论证
topic：讨论的主题，不等于观点
e.g.
Topic: social media
Thesis: Social media has had a negative impact on teenagers' attention spans.

Word Family / Formation:
thesis n. 论点；学位论文
theses n. thesis 的复数 /ˈθiːsiːz/

Usage Note:
本文 prove my thesis 中 thesis 指“论点/主张”，不是“学位论文”。
records.examples: thesis: Mr Ponta has also been accused of plagiarising his PhD thesis and lying in his CV. [https://www.economist.com/europe/2012/12/15/clear-victory-uncertain-future]
records.definitionEn: A central claim or opinion that is developed logically and supported with evidence; here, the author's main claim about university education.
records.otherSensesEn: 1) A long research-based piece of writing completed as part of a university degree, especially a master's or doctoral degree.

records.definition: 用具体事例说明或阐明。本文指作者的个人经历能够说明他的论点。
records.otherSenses:
1) 给书、文章等配插图
2) 表明某事属实或某种情况确实存在
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
illustrate a point 说明一个观点
illustrate an idea/concept 阐明一个想法/概念
illustrate sth with an example 用例子说明……
be illustrated with pictures 配有图片

Contrast:
illustrate：用例子、事实或图像把意思讲清楚；适合把抽象观点变具体
exemplify：某个事物本身就是一类事物的典型实例；常用作 be exemplified by
demonstrate：通过过程、实验或证据展示“如何做／确实如此”
explain：说明原因、原理、步骤或逻辑；不一定需要实例
clarify：消除模糊或误解，把已经提出的意思说得更清楚
elaborate on：在已有观点上补充细节与展开说明
substantiate：用证据支持某项主张；语气比 illustrate 更正式

Word Family / Formation:
illustrate v. 说明；加插图
illustration n. 说明；插图
illustrative adj. 说明性的
illustrator n. 插画师

Usage Note:
本文 illustrate 表示“说明/阐明”，不是“给书刊画插图”。
records.examples: illustrate: He uses both authors to illustrate how, by the early 19th century, it was logical to disdain work in favour of marrying into wealth.  [https://www.theguardian.com/books/2014/apr/28/thomas-piketty-capital-surprise-bestseller]
records.definitionEn: To make an idea or argument clear by using an example; here, the author's personal experience helps explain and support his thesis.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) To provide a book, article or other text with pictures.
2) To show that something is true or that a particular situation exists.

records.definition: 设法绕过或避开困难、限制。本文指避开教师、同学和使思想定型的大学制度所造成的阻碍。
records.otherSenses:
1) 四处走动；从一处到另一处
2) 到许多地方旅行
3) 消息等传播开来
4) 说服某人同意或按自己的想法办事
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
get around a problem 设法绕过问题
get around a rule 规避规则
get around an obstacle 绕过障碍

Contrast:
get around：绕开问题，不一定真正解决
avoid：直接避开、不接触
bypass：绕过某个具体程序、系统或障碍，较正式
circumvent：设法规避规则/限制，正式，常带“钻空子”意味
overcome：真正克服、解决困难

Word Family / Formation:
get v. 得到；变得
around adv. / prep. 在周围；绕过

Usage Note:
💡
get around a problem ≠ solve a problem
前者是“绕过去”，后者是“解决掉”
get around a law/rule 常可能带负面含义：规避规定、钻漏洞
get around to sth / doing sth 是另一个固定短语：终于抽出时间做某事
records.examples: get around: In order to get around the limitation rule, he sent his illiterate manservant off to the British Museum to find a copy of the Weekly Dispatch article published some 17 years previously. [https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/libertycentral/2009/sep/24/multiple-publication-libel-tourists]
records.definitionEn: To find a way of avoiding or overcoming a problem, rule or restriction; here, to bypass obstacles created by the faculty, other students and the college system.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) To move from place to place, especially despite difficulty.
2) To travel to many different places.
3) For news or information, to become widely known or circulate.
4) To persuade someone to agree with you or do what you want.

records.definition: （美式英语）大学的全体教师。本文指学生需要设法绕过的教师群体。
records.otherSenses:
1) （英式英语）大学中由若干相关院系组成的学部、学院
2) 人的某种天生能力或官能，如理解力、视力
3) faculties（复数）：正常的思考、感知和行动能力
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
faculty members 大学教师
university/college faculty 大学教师群体
the Faculty of Arts/Science 文学院/理学院
mental faculties 心智能力
lose one’s faculties 丧失正常思考或感知能力

Contrast:
faculty：大学教师群体；也可指学院
staff：员工总称，范围更广，不只教师
department：系/部门，通常比 faculty 更小
school：学院/学部，具体层级因大学而异
ability：一般“能力”；faculty 更正式，常指天生或基本能力

Word Family / Formation:
faculty n. 教师群体；学院；官能
faculties n. faculty 的复数；常指心智能力

Usage Note:
美式英语 faculty 指大学全体教师，不包括所有行政、后勤人员；staff 的范围更广。
将群体看作整体可用单数；强调成员时可用复数，英式英语更常如此。为清楚起见可写 The faculty members are ...。
“学院”义的层级因大学而异，不能断言 faculty 一定比 school 大或小。
records.examples: faculty: First, student protesters are backed by faculty and parents. [https://www.economist.com/britain/2003/03/06/dream-on]
records.definitionEn: In American English, the teaching staff of a college or university; here, the university teachers whom the student must learn to navigate around.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) In British English, a university division made up of related departments.
2) A natural mental or physical ability, such as the faculty of sight or reason.
3) faculties (plural): a person's normal powers of thinking, sensing and acting.

records.definition: 使思想定型、把人的思考限制在既定框架内。它是作者在本文语境中构成的批评性表达。
records.otherSenses:
1) mind：头脑；思维能力
2) mind：想法、意见或意愿
3) fixing：固定、使不再改变；在其他语境还可指修理或安排
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
fixed ways of thinking 固定的思维方式
independent thinking 独立思考
think outside the box 跳出固有思路（惯用语）

Contrast:
mind-fixing：作者用来批评思想被定型的语境表达
conformity：顺从群体规范，未必由强制导致
indoctrination：把某套信念灌输给人并限制质疑
rigid thinking：思维方式僵化，不说明成因

Word Family / Formation:
mind n. 头脑；思想
fix v. 使固定；修理
fixed adj. 固定的；不变的

Usage Note:
fix 在这里表示“使固定”，不是“修理”。这个带批判意味的临时复合词应结合全文理解，不当作现代高频搭配背诵。
records.examples:
John Stuart Mill observes: "Those only are happy who have their minds fixed on some object other than their own happiness … Aiming thus at something else, they find happiness along the way".
[https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/belief/2011/aug/08/christianity-us-collapsing-america]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries — mind（mind-fixing 无独立词条）
records.definitionEn: A context-specific compound meaning the process of fixing people's minds within accepted patterns and limiting independent thought.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) mind: the part of a person that enables awareness, thought and feeling, or the ability to think and reason.
2) mind: a person's thoughts, opinion, intention or will.
3) fixing: the act of making something firm or unable to change; in other contexts, repairing something or arranging a matter.

records.definition: 学位；完成大学课程后获得的学历资格。
records.otherSenses:
1) 程度；等级
2) 温度的度数
3) 角度的度数
4) 【语法】形容词或副词的级
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
get/earn a degree 获得学位
a bachelor's/master's/doctoral degree 学士/硕士/博士学位
to some/a certain degree 在某种程度上
to a large/great degree 在很大程度上
30 degrees 30度

Contrast:
degree：完成大学学业后授予的学位
diploma：证明完成特定课程的文凭，具体级别因地区而异
certificate：证书的统称，不一定代表大学学位
qualification：资格或资历，可包含学位和证书

Word Family / Formation:
degree n. 学位；程度；度
degree holder n. 学位持有者

Usage Note:
学位是可数的：a degree in history。
degree 也可表示程度或度数；degree of certainty 是“确定程度”，不指学位。
to a certain degree 表示“在一定程度上”；通常不写 to certain degree。
records.examples: degree: He admitted that when the virus first struck "there was probably a lack of knowledge and there was a certain degree of arrogance", but he said he believed lessons were being learned. [https://app.ludwig.guru/s/degree]
records.definitionEn: An academic qualification awarded after successfully completing a course of study at a university or college.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) The amount, level or extent of something.
2) A unit used to measure temperature.
3) A unit used to measure angles.
4) Grammar: one of the forms used to compare adjectives or adverbs, such as positive, comparative and superlative.

records.definition: 具有某种价值。本文 not worth so much as 表示“价值不如……”，即学位不及学习能力和动力重要。
records.otherSenses:
1) 值某个金额或数量
2) 值得花时间、精力或采取行动，常用 be worth doing
3) 【名词】价值；重要性；个人或事物的价值
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
be worth + money 值多少钱
be worth + n. 值得……
be worth doing 值得做
be well worth doing 非常值得做
be worth it 值得

Contrast:
worth：强调“做这件事值不值”，关注投入与回报
be worth doing / be worth the money
worthwhile：强调“这件事本身有没有价值、意义”
a worthwhile experience / The activity is worthwhile.
worthy：强调“是否配得上某种认可、尊重或关注”
be worthy of respect/attention/praise

Word Family / Formation:
worthwhile adj. 值得花时间或精力的
worthy adj. 值得尊敬或关注的
worthless adj. 无价值的
self-worth n. 自我价值感
net worth n. 净资产

Usage Note:
worth 通常用于 be worth ...，不直接放在名词前；后接名词、代词、金额或 doing，不用 worth to do。
The book is worth reading. 这本书值得读。这里 book 是 read 的逻辑宾语，doing 用主动形式表达被动关系。
本文 not worth so much as 比较价值，意思是“不如……有价值”。
records.examples: worth: Teddy Roosevelt once observed that life's greatest gift is the opportunity to work hard at work worth doing. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/nov/09/barack-obama-debt-deal-live]
records.definitionEn: Having a particular value or importance; here, not worth so much as means that a degree is less valuable than the capacity and drive to learn.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Having a monetary or measurable value equal to a stated amount.
2) Deserving the time, effort or action involved, commonly in the pattern be worth doing.
3) Noun: the value, importance or usefulness of a person or thing.

records.definition: 和……一样多或一样有价值；本文用于否定比较 not worth so much as，表示“不如……有价值”。
records.otherSenses:
1) as much as + 数量：多达……；用于强调数量之大
2) not so much as + 动作：甚至连……都没有
3) as much as to say：等于说；仿佛在说
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
not so ... as ... 不如……那么……
not worth as much as ... 不如……有价值（现代常见表达）

Contrast:
so much as 常见三种结构
not so much as + V = 甚至连……都不
He didn't so much as look at me.
not so much A as B = 与其说A，不如说B
It was not so much a failure as a lesson.
not ... so much as ... = 不如……那么…… / 没有……那么多；本质：not as much as
A degree is not worth so much as the capacity and drive to learn.
= A degree is not worth as much as the capacity and drive to learn.
学位没有学习能力和学习动力那么有价值。

Word Family / Formation:
much det. / pron. / adv. 很多；很大程度
more det. / pron. / adv. 更多；much 的比较级
most det. / pron. / adv. 最多；much 的最高级

Usage Note:
本文是 not [worth so much as ...] 的价值比较，相当于 not worth as much as。
not so much A as B 表示“与其说 A，不如说 B”，比较哪个描述更准确。
not so much as + 动词表示“甚至连……也不”，如 He did not so much as look up. 他甚至没有抬头。
三者的否定范围不同，不能只看相邻的 so much as 就套用同一种解释。
records.examples: so/as much as: Understand it's never worth as much as you think it is, and from a personal perspective, it's not worth it at all. [https://www.theguardian.com/media/2002/oct/01/comment]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries — much（so/as much as 无独立词条）
records.definitionEn: Used to compare value, amount or degree; here, not worth so much as means not as valuable as.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) as much as + an amount: up to that amount, often emphasizing that it is surprisingly large.
2) not so much as + verb: not even doing the stated action.
3) as much as to say: having the effect of saying or suggesting something.

records.definition: 理解或做某事的能力、潜能。本文 the capacity to learn 指学习能力。
records.otherSenses:
1) 容器或空间可容纳的数量；容量
2) 工厂、机器等的生产能力
3) 某人的正式身份、职位或作用
4) 发动机等设备的容积或功率
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
the capacity to do sth 做某事的能力
have the capacity for sth 有……的能力
production capacity 生产能力
seating/storage capacity 容纳量/储存量
in one's capacity as ... 以……身份

Contrast:
capacity：潜在或实际“能够做到”的能力，较正式
ability：最普通的“能力”
capability：强调具备完成某任务的本领/功能
competence：强调达到合格标准的胜任能力
potential：潜力，尚未完全发挥

Word Family / Formation:
capable adj. 有能力的
capability n. 能力；性能
incapable adj. 无能力的
incapacity n. 无能力；失能

Usage Note:
capacity to do sth 表示做某事的能力；be capable of doing sth 中 of 是介词。
capacity for sth 可指容纳能力或某种潜能；at full capacity 是“满负荷”。
in one’s capacity as ... 表示“以……身份”，此处 capacity 不作“能力”解。
records.examples: capacity: For someone who woke up at 1.30am in Germany, her capacity for exuberant chatter is remarkable.[https://www.theguardian.com/music/2011/oct/20/kelly-clarkson-stronger-american-idol]
records.definitionEn: The ability or potential to understand or do something; here, the ability to learn.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) The amount that a container, space or place can hold.
2) The maximum amount that a factory, machine or system can produce or process.
3) A particular official position, role or function in which someone acts.
4) The size, volume or power of an engine or other piece of equipment.

records.definition: 实现目标的强烈动力、干劲和决心。本文指持续学习的内在动力。
records.otherSenses:
1) 驾车行程；乘车旅行
2) 为某一目标开展的有组织活动或运动
3) 计算机的驱动器或存储设备
4) 通向住宅或建筑物的私人车道
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
the drive to do sth 做某事的动力
have the drive to succeed 有成功的动力
inner drive 内在驱动力
be driven by sth 受……驱动
drive sb to do sth 驱使某人做某事

Contrast:
drive：持续推动人行动的内在动力
motivation：做某事的动机/积极性，范围更广
ambition：想取得成就、地位的强烈愿望
determination：下定决心后坚持到底
incentive：外部激励，如奖金、奖励

Word Family / Formation:
drive v. 驱动；推动
driven adj. 有强烈进取心的；受驱动的
driver n. 驾驶员；推动因素

Usage Note:
the drive to learn = 学习的内在动力
drive ≠ motivation
drive 更强调持续、强烈的内在推动力；motivation 更泛
driven 可形容人：
a highly driven person = 很有进取心的人
records.examples: drive: Back then they had vision, drive and the desire to make the world of education a better place. [https://www.theguardian.com/teacher-network/2015/mar/07/secret-teacher-school-managers]
records.definitionEn: Strong energy, determination and ambition that push someone to achieve a goal; here, the inner motivation to keep learning.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) A journey made in a car or other vehicle.
2) An organized effort or campaign to achieve a particular purpose.
3) A computer device used to store or read data.
4) A private road leading from a public road to a house or other building.

records.definition: 突然想到或偶然发现。本文 was hit on by accident 指这个方法是偶然想出来的。
records.otherSenses: 1) hit on somebody（非正式）：向某人调情或作出性暗示
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
hit on an idea 想到一个主意
hit on a solution 想到解决办法
hit on the answer 想到答案
hit on sb 搭讪某人；向某人示好

Contrast:
hit on：偶然/突然想到
come up with：想出，最常用，不一定强调“突然”
think of：想到，最普通
figure out：经过思考后弄明白/解决
stumble on/upon：偶然发现，强调“碰巧发现”

Word Family / Formation:
hit v. 击中；达到
hit v. hit 的过去式和过去分词
hitting v. hit 的现在分词

Usage Note:
本文 My method was hit on ... 使用了被动式，on 保留，表示“这个方法是偶然想到的”。
Oxford 将现代“想到主意”义的 hit on/upon sth 标为不用于被动；这里保留作者原句，现代仿写优先用 I hit on an idea. 我偶然想到一个主意。
hit on sb 是美式俚语“与某人搭讪／调情”，须与 hit on an idea 区分。
records.examples: hit on: She hit on a scheme.[https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/1951/08/25/musicale]
records.definitionEn: To think of or discover an idea, method or solution suddenly or by chance; here, the author's method was found accidentally.
records.otherSensesEn: 1) hit on somebody (informal): to speak or behave toward someone in a way that shows sexual or romantic interest.

records.definition: 偶然地；并非有意或事先计划。本文说明作者并非有意识地设计出这个方法。
records.otherSenses:
1) accident：造成伤害或损失的意外事件、事故
2) accident：偶然发生的事情；非计划因素
3) an accident of history/geography：历史或地理上的偶然结果
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
happen by accident 偶然发生
discover/find sth by accident 偶然发现某事
quite/purely by accident 完全出于偶然

Contrast:
by accident：无意中、并非故意
accidentally：副词形式，表示“偶然地；无意地”
by chance：强调碰巧发生或偶然遇到
on purpose：故意地，与 by accident 相反

Usage Note:
by accident 通常放在句末，说明某事并非有意为之。本文 hit on by accident 表示“偶然想到”，重点是方法并非预先设计。
records.examples: by accident: It could not have happened by accident. [https://www.newyorker.com/news/hendrik-hertzberg/heritage-diagnosed-severe-demintia].
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries — accident（by accident 无独立词条）
records.definitionEn: By chance and without intention or advance planning; here, the method was not consciously designed.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) accident: an unexpected event, especially one causing injury or damage.
2) accident: something that happens by chance rather than by design.
3) an accident of history/geography: a result produced by historical or geographical chance rather than deliberate planning.

records.definition: 未经有意识推理而引导行动的本能或直觉。本文指某种直觉也促成了作者的方法。
records.otherSenses:
1) 动物或人生来就有的行为倾向
2) 对某事的自然感觉或直觉判断
3) 做某事的天赋、自然能力
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
by instinct 凭本能
follow/trust one's instincts 相信自己的直觉
instinct for sth 对……的天生感觉/天赋
survival instinct 生存本能
maternal instinct 母性本能

Contrast:
instinct：本能或未经理性分析产生的判断
intuition：直觉判断，强调“凭感觉知道”
impulse：一时冲动，强调突然想做某事
reflex：反射动作，通常是身体自动反应

Word Family / Formation:
instinct n. 本能；直觉
instinctive adj. 本能的；直觉的
instinctively adv. 本能地；下意识地

Usage Note:
trust your instincts 很常用 = 相信你的直觉
have an instinct for sth = 对某事有天生的感觉/才能
instinct 不一定指动物本能，也常用于人的判断：
My first instinct was to say no.
records.examples: instinct: My instinct when I look at this photo is to grab that girl and protect her, her social awkwardness, in the same way I want to protect my little girl who is six and identical to me. [https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2023/mar/04/jessie-cave-looks-back]
records.definitionEn: A natural feeling that guides action without conscious reasoning; here, an intuitive impulse that helped produce the author's method.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) An inborn tendency that makes a person or animal behave in a particular way without learning or training.
2) A natural feeling or judgment that something is true even without facts or conscious reasoning.
3) A natural talent or ability for a particular activity.

records.definition: 专攻某一学科或领域。本文简短地说明作者把学习集中到自己真正感兴趣的方向。
records.otherSenses:
1) 企业或从业者专门生产、销售或提供某类产品或服务
2) 【生物】细胞、器官等演化成具有特定功能的形态
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
specialize in sth 专攻/专门从事……
specialize in doing sth 专门做……
a company specializing in... 一家专门从事……的公司

Contrast:
specialize in：长期专注于某一专业领域
focus on：把注意力集中在……，范围更广
concentrate on：集中精力做某事
major in：大学主修某专业
be engaged in：从事……，不强调专业化

Word Family / Formation:
special adj. 特别的
specialist n. 专家；专科医生
specialized adj. 专门的；专业化的
specialization n. 专业化；专门领域

Usage Note:
✅ specialize in sth/doing
❌ specialize on
records.examples: specialize: The priests specialize in arrogance, the nuns in humility.As for the nuns themselves, some have declined to comment, because they have to be obedient. [https://www.economist.com/democracy-in-america/2012/04/26/nuns-gone-wild]
records.definitionEn: To focus one's study on a particular subject or field and develop special expertise in it; here, the student concentrates on the area that genuinely interests him.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) For a business or professional, to concentrate on producing, selling or providing a particular type of product or service.
2) In biology, for a cell, organ or organism to develop a particular form or function.

records.definition: 正式规定、指定。本文 several courses prescribed 指学校规定必须修读的几门课程。
records.otherSenses:
1) 医生开具处方或规定治疗方法
2) 规章、法律等规定应采取的行为或程序
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
prescribe medicine/drugs 开药
prescribe sth for sb 给某人开……
prescribe sth for a condition 针对某病症开……
prescribe rules/procedures 规定规则/程序
as prescribed 按规定

Contrast:
prescribe：正式规定“应该做什么”；医学上指“开处方”
recommend：建议，不具强制性
require：要求，强调必须做到
stipulate：明确规定条款/条件，法律或合同语境更常见

Word root · scrib/script:
scrib(e) / script 源自拉丁语 scribere，核心义是“写”。
prescribe = pre-（预先）+ scribe：预先写下规定 → 开处方／正式规定
describe = de-（写下、展开）+ scribe：描述
inscribe = in-（写入）+ scribe：题写；刻写
subscribe = sub-（在下方）+ scribe：签名认购；订阅
script：写成的文字；剧本
scripture：宗教经典文本
scribe：抄写员；书记员

Word Family / Formation:
prescription n. 处方；规定
prescribed adj. 规定的；处方指定的
prescriptive adj. 规定性的；指令性的

Usage Note:
本文 prescribed courses 指学校规定修读的课程；不是开药义。
prescribe a treatment 是“规定治疗”；describe a treatment 是“描述治疗”，两词不要混淆。
核心：由具有相应权力或专业资格的人规定应做什么。
records.examples: prescribe: For example, the clinician could decide to see the patient more frequently or prescribe a different medication. [https://www.economist.com/lexingtons-notebook/2013/03/13/why-the-nra-keeps-talking-about-mental-illness-rather-than-guns]
records.definitionEn: To state officially that something must be done, used or followed; here, the university formally requires certain courses.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) For a doctor or other qualified professional, to order a particular medicine or treatment for a patient.
2) For a law, rule or authority, to state formally which action or procedure must be followed.

records.definition: 把注意力、时间或精力集中在……上。本文指作者重点学习最感兴趣的一两门课程。
records.otherSenses:
1) concentrate something：把人力、资源等集中到一处或一个目标
2) concentrate a substance：除去液体等使物质浓缩
3) concentrate（名词）：浓缩物；浓缩液
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
concentrate on sth 专注于某事
concentrate on doing sth 集中精力做某事
concentrate one’s efforts on sth 把精力集中在……

Contrast:
concentrate on：主动集中精力，减少分心
focus on：把注意力或讨论的重点放在某处
specialize in：长期专门从事某个领域

Word Family / Formation:
concentrate v. 集中（注意力）
concentration n. 专注；集中；浓度
concentrated adj. 集中的；浓缩的

Usage Note:
on 是介词，后接名词或 doing，不能写 concentrate on to do。
本文 on the one or two 中省略 courses；that interested me most 修饰这些课程。
records.examples: For the first time I did not need a Saturday job. I could concentrate on my studies and write for the Newcastle University student newspaper. [https://www.theguardian.com/education/2022/apr/17/poorer-students-will-bear-the-brunt-of-costly-loans]
records.definitionEn: To direct one's attention, time or effort toward a particular subject or activity; here, to give most attention to the one or two most interesting courses.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) concentrate something: to bring people, resources or activity together in one place or direct them toward one aim.
2) concentrate a substance: to remove liquid or other material so that the substance becomes stronger or denser.
3) concentrate (noun): a substance from which water or another component has been removed.

records.definition: 集中而深入地；以高强度投入。本文指作者对最喜欢的课程下了很大功夫。
records.otherSenses:
1) 密集地使用土地、劳动力或资源，如 intensively farmed land
2) 在短时间内集中训练或治疗，如 study/train intensively
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
study/train/work intensively 集中、高强度地学习/训练/工作
investigate/research sth intensively 深入调查/研究某事
use sth intensively 高频、高强度使用某物

Contrast:
intensively：强调投入密集、强度高；常涉及较短时间或较小范围，但不限定总时长
intently：强调注意力高度集中
extensively：强调范围广，不是强度高
thoroughly：强调做得彻底、全面

Word Family / Formation:
intensive adj. 密集的；强化的
intense adj. 强烈的
intensity n. 强度
intensify v. 加强；加剧
intensification n. 加强；加剧

Usage Note:
intensively 强调投入密集；intently 强调注意力集中；extensively 强调范围广。
intensive 常描述工作、训练等安排；intense 常描述感受、光线、压力等强烈程度。
time-intensive 是形容词，意为“耗时的”；它不等于副词 intensively。
records.examples: intensively: Both sides have been intensively preparing for what each says will be a "decisive" second round.Such a war would bear little resemblance to the previous clashes between Israel and its neighbours. [https://www.economist.com/leaders/2010/12/29/please-not-again]
records.definitionEn: With concentrated effort and a high level of activity; here, the student studies the chosen courses very deeply and energetically.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) By making dense or heavy use of land, labour or other resources, as in intensively farmed land.
2) In a concentrated way over a limited period, as in intensive study, training or treatment.

records.definition: （美式英语）大学三年级的。本文 junior year 指四年制大学的第三学年。
records.otherSenses:
1) 职位或级别较低的；资历较浅的
2) 年龄较小的；晚辈的
3) 【名词，美式英语】大学三年级学生
4) 【名词】同名父子中较年轻者，常写作 Junior 或 Jr.
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
junior staff/employee 初级员工
junior position/role 初级职位
be junior to sb 职位/资历低于某人
be X years junior to sb 比某人小 X 岁
a college junior 大学三年级学生（美）

Contrast:
junior：等级/资历较低，相对概念
entry-level：入门级，强调职业起点
inexperienced：经验不足，强调实际经验
young：年龄小
subordinate：下属的，强调上下级从属关系

Word Family / Formation:
junior adj. / n. 较低级的；三年级学生
senior adj. / n. 较高级的；四年级学生（对应词）
seniority n. 资历；年资（相关词）

本文 junior year 中 junior 作形容词，指四年制大学的三年级；a college junior 才是“大三学生”。
美式典型四年顺序：freshman → sophomore → junior → senior。
职位或资历比较用 junior to，不用 junior than；年龄差可写 He is two years my junior.
records.examples: junior: To date, only one cabinet minister and a few junior officials have been arrested. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2014/may/20/malawi-election-2014-not-perfect-but-good-start]
records.definitionEn: In American English, relating to the third year of a four-year college course; here, junior year means the student's third academic year.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Lower in rank, status or experience.
2) Younger than another person.
3) Noun, American English: a student in the third year of a four-year high school or college course.
4) Noun: the younger of two people with the same name, often written Junior or Jr.

records.definition: 容易完成或通过的事情。本文 several cinches in history 是早期美国校园用语，指几门很容易通过的历史课或要求。
records.otherSenses:
1) 十拿九稳的事；确定无疑的结果
2) 【马术】固定马鞍的肚带
3) 【动词】把某事牢牢系紧或确保成功
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
be a cinch 轻而易举
a cinch to do sth 很容易做某事
an easy cinch 容易通过的课程／项目（旧式校园俚语）

Contrast:
a cinch：容易的事；在早期校园语境中也可指轻松的课程或宽松教师
a snap：容易的事；可作 cinch 的近义校园俚语
a soft course：要求较低、容易通过的课程
an academic warning：学业警告；不是 cinch 本身的常规词义
clinch：动词，指敲定或赢得；注意多一个 l

Word Family / Formation:
cinch n. 容易的事；马鞍肚带
cinch v. 束紧；确保获得（非正式）

Usage Note:
已核实：美国国会图书馆保存的 1913 年资料把大学中“容易的课程”称为 softs、snaps 或 cinches；1902 年的大学俚语资料也把 cinch 用于宽松教师或容易的课程。
因此本文 several cinches in history 指历史课中有几门容易的课／要求较低的课，而不是“收到数份学业警告”。后来的 cinch notice 确实可指预警通知，但那是另一个固定搭配，不能倒推本句词义。
clinch a deal 是“敲定交易”；cinch a belt 是“束紧腰带”。
records.examples: cinch: The apparently daunting task of arguing that the economy is stronger yet still too weak for giveaways turned out to be a cinch. [https://www.economist.com/britain/2014/03/20/general-osborne]
records.definitionEn: Something that is very easy; here, an easy history course or academic requirement requiring little effort.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Something certain to happen, or a person certain to succeed
2) A strap around a horse's body that holds the saddle in place
3) Verb: to fasten something tightly or make an outcome certain

records.definition: 没有给予应有的注意或投入；忽视。本文指作者此前没有认真学习历史。
records.otherSenses:
1) 没有妥善照顾某人、健康或财产
2) neglect to do something：疏忽或忘记做本应做的事
3) 【名词】缺少应有的照顾或关注；疏忽
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
neglect one's duties 玩忽职守
neglect a child/patient 疏于照顾孩子/病人
neglect to do sth 忘记/疏忽做某事
suffer from neglect 因疏于照顾而受损
through neglect 由于疏忽

Contrast:
neglect：没有给予应有的照顾或重视，可出于疏忽，也可有意不重视
ignore：不予理会，常强调有意识地不回应
overlook：在“漏看”义上强调没注意到；另可表示不追究过错
disregard：不把规则、建议等纳入考虑，较正式

Word Family / Formation:
neglectful adj. 疏忽的；疏于照顾的
neglected adj. 被忽视的；缺乏照顾的
negligence n. 疏忽；失职
negligent adj. 疏忽的；失职的

Usage Note:
常用 neglect to do sth：疏忽或未尽责而没做某事，不一定真的忘记。He neglected to reply. 他疏于回复。
表示没有完成本该做的事，通常优先用 neglect to do；不要机械套用 doing。
neglect 可出于疏忽，也可有意识地不重视；ignore 更直接表示不理会，二者不是“必然无意”与“必然有意”的绝对二分。
本文 I had neglected it 指此前未给历史足够重视；名词 neglect 为不可数。
records.examples: neglect: When a child dies of neglect or abuse, the local authority is accused of incompetence and negligence; if there is an outbreak of foot and mouth disease, claims about inadequate precautions are heard; former employees of companies which have collapsed during the recession demand to know why more has not been done to save their jobs. [https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2009/aug/21/obama-healthcare-britain-recession-government]
records.definitionEn: To fail to give something the attention it needs; here, to have given too little attention to the study of history.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) To fail to take proper care of a person, one's health or property
2) neglect to do something: to fail or forget to do something that ought to be done
3) Noun: the failure to give somebody or something enough care or attention

records.definition: 对某种做法强烈抵触并拒绝接受。本文指作者反感把历史教成与现实生活割裂的固定知识。
records.otherSenses:
1) rebel against：反抗政府、权威、规则或传统
2) 【名词】反叛者；反抗权威的人
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
rebel against sb/sth 反抗……
rebel against authority 反抗权威
rebel against convention 反抗传统
rebel forces 叛军
a teenage rebel 叛逆少年

Contrast:
rebel：反抗权威、制度、传统，带“反叛”色彩
resist：抵抗、不接受，范围更广
protest：公开抗议某事
revolt：起义、暴动，程度通常更强
defy：公然违抗命令、规则或权威

Word Family / Formation:
rebellion n. 反叛；叛乱
rebellious adj. 反叛的；叛逆的
rebelliously adv. 反叛地

Usage Note:
名词 /ˈrebəl/ 重音在前；动词 /rɪˈbel/ 重音在后。过去式 rebelled、现在分词 rebelling 都双写 l。
反抗权威、规则时常用 rebel against；本文 rebelled at the way ... 表示对那种教学方式产生抵触，保留作者的 at。
rebellious 也可形容日常生活中叛逆、不服管的人，不一定涉及政治叛乱。
records.examples: rebel: The failure here was not being knocked out but the way it happened; the fact they did not rebel against their fate.[https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/apr/21/barcelona-paris-saint-germain-champions-league-match-report]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries — rebel（rebel at 无独立词条）
records.definitionEn: To react strongly against and refuse to accept a practice or situation; here, to resist a way of teaching history as fixed facts disconnected from life.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) rebel against: to fight against or refuse to obey a government, authority, rule or tradition
2) Noun: a person who fights against or refuses to obey authority

records.definition: 被当作确定、已经成立的事实来传授的知识。本文含批评意味，指历史被教成孤立而不可质疑的事实。
records.otherSenses:
1) positive：积极的；有益的
2) positive：确信的；明确无疑的
3) positive：检测结果为阳性的
4) positive：【数学】正数的；大于零的
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
positive knowledge 被视为确定的知识（本文）
established facts 已确立的事实
factual knowledge 事实性知识

Contrast:
positive knowledge：本文指被当作既定事实教授的知识
factual knowledge：关于事实的知识，不一定排斥质疑
empirical knowledge：以观察或经验为依据的知识，强调来源

Word Family / Formation:
know v. 知道；了解
knowledge n. 知识
knowledgeable adj. 知识丰富的

Usage Note:
positive 此处取“确定、确实”义，不是“积极、正能量”。
这不是应机械背诵的现代常见固定短语，也不要仅凭这个短语就认定作者在讲某一哲学学派。
knowledge 通常不可数；可写 a body of knowledge，不写 a knowledge 来表示“一条知识”。
records.examples: postive knowledge: Positive knowledge of languages and history was necessary, but it was never enough, any more than the mechanical gathering of facts would constitute an adequate method for grasping what an author like Dante, for example, was all about. [https://www.theguardian.com/books/2003/aug/02/alqaida.highereducation]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries — positive（positive knowledge 无独立词条）
records.definitionEn: Knowledge presented as certain, established fact; here, historical information taught as isolated facts that are not open to question.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) positive: good, useful or beneficial
2) positive: completely certain or definite
3) positive: showing that a medical test has detected what it was looking for
4) positive: greater than zero in mathematics

records.definition: 与……没有联系。本文指课堂中的历史知识被处理成与政治、艺术和生活毫不相干。
records.otherSenses: 1) unrelated：彼此没有亲属关系的
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
be unrelated to sth 与……无关
seemingly/apparently unrelated 看似无关的
two unrelated events 两个互不相关的事件
unrelated individuals 无亲属关系的人

records.definition: 在思维、推理和理解层面。本文 intellectually need 指在理解和思想探索上真正需要。

本文 this memorandum 回指教授列出的参考资料，不是作者的记忆力。
records.examples: memorandum: The Scottish and UK governments will draw up and agree a memorandum of understanding to ensure that devolution is not detrimental to UK-wide critical national infrastructure in relation to matters such as defence and security, oil and gas and energy. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2014/nov/27/scottish-devolution-smith-commission-key-points]
records.definitionEn: A written note or record kept for future reference; here, the professor's list of additional references or reading.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) A formal note sent within an organization
2) Law: a record of an agreement that has not yet been formally drawn up and signed
3) A document giving proposals or a report on a particular subject to a person, organization or committee

records.definition: 在某个问题或观点上存在差异、意见不一致。本文指两本书在若干问题上的说法不同。
records.otherSenses:
1) differ from：与另一人或事物不同
2) differ in：在某个方面有差异
3) differ with somebody：与某人意见不合
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
differ on several points 在若干点上意见不同
differ on how to proceed 对如何推进看法不同

Contrast:
differ on：对某议题的观点不同
differ from：两个事物在特征上不同
disagree with：与某人或某种意见不一致

Usage Note:
本文主语是 two different books，differed on several points 指书中叙述或立场在若干点上不同。on 后接争议的议题；不能把 differ on sb 用来表示“不同意某人”。
records.examples: differ on: Realists differ on how much power is enough. [https://app.ludwig.guru/s/differ+on]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries — differ（differ on 无独立词条）
records.definitionEn: To have different opinions or accounts concerning a particular issue; here, for two books to give different views on several points.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) differ from: to be different from another person or thing
2) differ in: to be different in a particular respect
3) differ with somebody: to disagree with that person

records.definition: 在某一领域被公认为可靠的权威资料或著作。本文 the other authorities 指作者继续查阅的其他权威来源。
records.otherSenses:
1) 发号施令的权力或管辖权
2) 做某事的法定权利或正式许可
3) authorities（复数）：当局；主管机构
4) 某领域的权威专家
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a leading authority on history 历史领域的权威
consult an authority 查阅权威资料
local authorities 地方当局
have the authority to do sth 有权做某事

Contrast:
authority：本文指可靠的专家或资料，也可指权力／当局
source：信息来源，未必具有权威性
evidence：支持结论的证据

Usage Note:
Turning to the other authorities 中 authorities 是复数，指其他可依凭的权威书籍或作者，不是政府部门。authority on + 领域 表示“某领域的权威”。
records.examples: authority: As president, Putin moved quickly to consolidate his authority over the economy and politics. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2014/jun/09/-sp-profiles-post-soviet-states]
records.definitionEn: A person or source whose knowledge or judgement is accepted as reliable; here, other authoritative writers or works consulted by the author.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) The power to give orders or exercise control
2) The legal right or official permission to do something
3) authorities: the people or organizations responsible for making decisions in a country or area
4) A person with expert knowledge of a particular subject

records.definition: 对某个问题持不同意见或有不同说法。本文指不同权威资料对同一批事实以及其他事实并不一致。
records.otherSenses:
1) disagree with somebody：不同意某人的观点
2) disagree that...：不接受某一说法为真
3) 某种食物、气候等 disagree with somebody：使某人不适
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
disagree on the facts 对事实的说法不同
disagree on a policy 对政策有分歧
disagree with sb about sth 与某人就某事意见不同

Contrast:
disagree on：突出分歧所在的议题
disagree with：突出意见相左的人或观点
differ on：较中性地说“在……方面不同”

Usage Note:
本文 they 指前面的 authorities；disagreed on the same facts 是“对同一批事实的解释或记载不一致”，不表示事实本身发生改变。
records.examples: disagree on: Disagreement between us is nothing new – we disagree on a lot of things and that’s OK. [https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2016/feb/20/a-letter-to-my-mother-who-wont-accept-we-dont-want-children]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries — disagree（disagree on 无独立词条）
records.definitionEn: To hold different opinions or give different accounts concerning an issue; here, for authorities to conflict over the same facts and additional facts.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) disagree with somebody: to have a different opinion from that person
2) disagree that...: to reject a statement as untrue
3) Food, weather, etc. disagrees with somebody: it makes that person feel ill

records.definition: 向某人恳求帮助；原句中的 appealed to 是省略式，表示“有人向这位图书管理员求助”。
records.otherSenses:
1) appeal to sb：吸引某人；使某人感兴趣
2) appeal against a decision：对判决或决定提出上诉
3) appeal to a principle/sense：诉诸某种原则、情感或判断
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
appeal to sb for help 向某人求助
appeal to sb to do sth 呼吁某人做某事
appeal to sb's interests 吸引某人的兴趣
appeal against a decision 对决定提出上诉
appeal to reason/common sense 诉诸理性／常识

Contrast:
appeal to sb for help：请求对方帮助或支持，常较恳切
ask sb for help：普通、中性的求助
consult sb：向对方征询专业意见

Word Family / Formation:
appeal v. / n. 请求；呼吁；上诉
appealing adj. 有吸引力的；恳求的
appealingly adv. 恳求地；有吸引力地

Usage Note:
The librarian, appealed to, ... 中 librarian 承受“被求助”的动作；appealed to 是补充性过去分词短语，可释为 when I appealed to the librarian。
to 是 appeal to 的组成部分，被动后仍保留。这个压缩表达较书面，不必作为现代口语模板。
appeal 的核心不是单一的“吸引”：搭配决定意思。The idea appeals to me 是“这个想法吸引我”；appeal against 则是“上诉”。
records.examples: appeal to sb for help: The widow of friendly fire victim Matty Hull today appealed to the US president for help in finding out the truth about her husband's death. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2007/mar/15/military.world]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: appeal（该完整搭配无独立页，链接父词条中的 appeal to somebody for something）
records.definitionEn: To make an earnest request to someone for help; in the original sentence, appealed to means that the librarian was asked for assistance.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) appeal to somebody: to attract or interest that person
2) appeal against a decision: to ask a court or authority to change it
3) appeal to a principle or feeling: to use it as the basis of a request or argument

records.definition: 短暂拜访某人；原句表示作者随后去拜访 Jones 教授。
records.otherSenses:
1) call on/upon sb to do sth：要求或敦促某人做某事
2) call on/upon sb：正式请某人发言
3) call：给某人打电话
4) call sb/sth：把某人或某物称为……
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
call on/upon sb 拜访某人
call on sb to do sth 正式要求某人做某事
call on a customer 拜访客户

Contrast:
call on sb：拜访某人，此义较正式
visit sb：普通的拜访；visit a place 也可指参观
drop in on sb：顺便、短暂拜访，较口语

Word Family / Formation:
call v. / n. 拜访；打电话；呼叫
caller n. 来访者；打电话的人

Usage Note:
拜访人用 call on sb；call at + 地点可表示到某处短暂停留，现代日常表达常直接用 visit。
call on sb to do sth 是呼吁／要求某人做某事；call sb 是打电话给某人，不能混为一谈。
records.examples: call on: However, I remember an embarrassing moment in New York, in 1989, when I called on Chinua Achebe at an NYU-run apartment block in which he was staying. [https://www.theguardian.com/books/2008/jul/22/keywords.novelists.lethem.thirlwell.farah.meek]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: call（“拜访”义列在父词条 visit 义项下；独立 call on 页主要收录“要求/请发言”）
records.definitionEn: To make a short visit to someone; in the source sentence, the writer then went to visit Professor Jones.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) call on/upon somebody to do something: to formally ask or urge someone to act.
2) call on/upon somebody: to formally invite someone to speak.
3) call somebody: to telephone someone.
4) call somebody/something + noun/adjective: to name or describe a person or thing in a particular way.

records.definition: 勤奋；勤勉。教授称赞的是作者查阅资料时表现出的用功和努力。
records.otherSenses:
1) 工业；以原材料制造产品的生产活动
2) 某一行业及其中的企业和人员，如 the film industry
3) 产业界；工业领域（不可数）
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
hard work and industry 勤奋努力
show great industry 表现得十分勤奋
an industrious student 勤奋的学生

Contrast:
industry：持续勤奋，此义正式，本文是对工作态度的评价
diligence：认真、细致且坚持不懈
productivity：产出的效率或数量，不等于勤奋
hard work：中性的“努力工作”

Word Family / Formation:
industry n. 勤奋；工业；行业
industrious adj. 勤奋的
industriously adv. 勤奋地
industrial adj. 工业的

Usage Note:
本文 industry 为不可数的“勤奋”。工业整体也通常不可数；某一行业可数，如 the film industry。
industrious 是“勤奋的”，industrial 是“工业的”，不要写 industrial student 来表示勤奋的学生。
approve my industry 在此是“赞许我的勤奋”；现代通常可说 approve of my diligence 或 praise my hard work。
records.examples: industry: His application, his industry, and his consistent diligence – astonished me. [https://www.theguardian.com/books/2016/aug/22/books-to-give-you-hope-prick-up-your-ears-by-john-lahr-joe-orton]
records.definitionEn: Steady hard work and diligence; the professor is praising the effort the writer put into researching the subject.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) The economic activity of producing goods from raw materials.
2) A particular area of business, together with the companies and people involved in it, such as the film industry.
3) Industry as a whole: the field of manufacturing and industrial business.

records.definition: 好奇的；求知欲强的。作者强调自己读书是因为真想弄明白问题。
records.otherSenses:
1) 奇怪的；不同寻常的
2) curious about/as to：对……感到好奇
3) curious to know/see：很想知道或看看
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
be curious about sth 对……好奇
be curious to know 想知道
a curious child 好奇的孩子
out of curiosity 出于好奇

Contrast:
curious：想弄清未知之事，强调求知欲
interested：对某事感兴趣，范围更广
inquisitive：爱追问、探究；也可能含“过分打听”的意味
strange：奇怪的，是 curious 的另一义

Word Family / Formation:
curious adj. 好奇的；奇怪的
curiosity n. 好奇心；奇物
curiously adv. 好奇地；奇怪地

Usage Note:
be curious about + 名词／疑问词从句；be curious to do sth 表示“很想知道而去做”。本文 a curious boy 与 a good boy 对照，意思是他的努力来自求知欲，不是为了表现乖巧。
records.examples: curious: Today's young people are inquisitive, curious and want their information to be easily digestible, as well as fun. [https://www.theguardian.com/higher-education-network/blog/2014/feb/17/how-to-recruit-attract-university-students]
records.definitionEn: Eager to learn, know or understand things; the writer stresses that he read because he truly wanted to find things out.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Strange or unusual.
2) curious about/as to something: wanting to know more about it.
3) curious to know/see: very interested in finding something out or seeing it.

records.definition: 难以解释、尚未得到答案的问题；这里指史料之间的矛盾反而使疑问更深。
records.otherSenses:
1) 神秘的人或事物；因了解很少而显得奇异
2) 神秘性；难以理解所产生的神秘气氛
3) 悬疑故事、电影或戏剧
4) 宗教中无法用科学解释的奥秘
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
solve a mystery 解开谜团
remain a mystery 仍是谜
deepen the mystery 加深谜团
be a mystery to sb 对某人是个谜

Contrast:
mystery：尚未得到解释的事
puzzle：令人困惑的问题或谜题
secret：被有意隐瞒的事

Word Family / Formation:
mystery n. 谜；未解之事
mysterious adj. 神秘的；难以解释的
mysteriously adv. 神秘地；不可思议地

Usage Note:
指一个未解问题时可数：a mystery；表示神秘感时用作不可数名词：an air of mystery。
本文不是指某个被故意隐瞒的秘密，而是尚待研究的历史问题。
mystery 的复数是 mysteries。
records.examples: mystery: To my genuine astonishment, I too find life is fine with only the essentials and what's in those boxes has become a mystery to me, although not an intriguing one. [https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2015/may/01/do-something-decluttering]
records.definitionEn: A question or situation that is difficult to explain and has not yet been answered; here, conflicting historical sources deepen the uncertainty.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) A person or thing that seems strange because little is known about them or it.
2) The quality or atmosphere of being difficult to understand.
3) A story, film or play about a puzzling event or crime.
4) A religious truth that cannot be explained by science or reason.

records.definition: 把问题解释清楚或解决；原句指书籍澄清了那个历史问题。
records.otherSenses:
1) （天气）转晴
2) （疾病、感染等）消失或痊愈
3) 清理、收拾，使地方整洁
4) 消除误会或困惑
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
clear up a mystery/problem 解开谜团／解决问题
clear up confusion/a misunderstanding 消除困惑／误会
clear an infection up 治好感染
the weather clears up 天气转晴

Contrast:
clear up：使问题、困惑或疾病消失；也可指天气转晴
clarify：把表达或信息讲得更清楚
resolve：彻底解决问题、争端或矛盾
clean up：清理、打扫；也可指整顿不良状况

Usage Note:
clear up 是可分短语动词：clear the problem up / clear it up。本文 clearing up the historical question 表示“把历史问题解释清楚”。
records.examples: clear up: Take antibiotics to clear up your infection. [https://www.wikihow.com/Recognize-Staph-Infection-Symptoms]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: clear up
records.definitionEn: To solve or explain a problem or mystery so that it becomes understood; in the source sentence, a book clarified the historical question.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Of weather: to become bright and free of cloud or rain.
2) Of an illness or infection: to disappear or be cured.
3) To make a place tidy by removing or putting away things.
4) To remove confusion or a misunderstanding.

records.definition: 强烈吸引；使着迷。原句的被动式表示作者被这种探索历史的方法深深吸引。
records.otherSenses:
1) 现代常用义基本都围绕“深深吸引、使非常感兴趣”展开
2) fascinated（形容人的感受）：着迷的
3) fascinating（形容事物的特点）：极有吸引力的
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
be fascinated by/with sth 对……着迷
be fascinated to learn/hear ... 得知／听到……而极感兴趣
fascination with sth 对……的着迷

Contrast:
fascinated：兴趣强烈，注意力被牢牢吸引
interested：想了解某事，范围最广
absorbed in：专注到很少注意周围
curious about：想弄清未知之事，强调求知欲

Word Family / Formation:
fascinate v. 使着迷
fascination n. 着迷；吸引力
fascinated adj. 着迷的
fascinating adj. 引人入胜的

Usage Note:
fascinated 描述感受；fascinating 描述造成这种感受的人或事：I am fascinated by a fascinating story。
分词形容词与被动常共享 be + -ed 形式，不能只看外形。若句子强调某事使某人产生反应，可读作被动：The audience was fascinated by the magician.；若它描述持续的心理状态，常作形容词理解：She remained fascinated. / He seems fascinated.
两种读法有时会重叠；by 短语、施事和事件过程支持被动，remain、seem、感受状态和上下文支持形容词。本句没有施事，重点是作者的状态，所以按系表结构标作分词形容词。
records.examples: fascinate: When it comes to Henry VIII the drama never seems to end, which is why his colourful life continues to fascinate us. [https://www.the-independent.com/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/wolf-hall-episode-5-tv-review-damian-lewis-is-so-good-as-the-capricious-king-that-you-want-to-slap-him-10054169.html]
records.definitionEn: To attract and hold someone's interest very strongly; the passive form in the source sentence shows that this way of exploring history deeply interested the writer.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Its usual modern sense is to attract and interest someone very strongly.
2) fascinated: extremely interested in something or someone.
3) fascinating: extremely interesting or attractive.

records.definition: 本质性的；根本的。essential differences 指观点和事实方面并非细枝末节的重大差异。
records.otherSenses:
1) 完全必要的；不可缺少的
2) 极其重要的
3) 最基本的；构成事物核心性质的
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
an essential difference 根本差异
the essential nature of sth 某事物的本质
be essential to/for sth 对……必不可少
the bare essentials 最基本的必需品

Contrast:
essential：本文强调涉及本质；另有不可缺少义
fundamental：作为基础或触及根本的
important：重要，但不一定根本或必要
necessary：为达到目的而必需

Word Family / Formation:
essence n. 本质；精髓
essential adj. 必要的；本质的
essentials n. 必需品；要点
essentially adv. 本质上；基本上

Usage Note:
essential differences 应按“根本／实质性差异”理解，不能译成“必要的差异”。
essential to/for 后接名词或 doing；It is essential to do sth 中 to 引出不定式。
essentially 常意为“本质上／基本上”，不是“一定要”。
records.examples: essential: "Intolerance of corruption is essential to the survival of our representative democracy and way of life," he said. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2015/feb/09/coal-approvals-must-be-overhauled-to-stop-corruption-says-former-nsw-watchdog]
records.definitionEn: Fundamental and central rather than minor; essential differences are major differences in viewpoints and facts.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Completely necessary for a particular purpose or situation.
2) Extremely important because it affects the result.
3) Forming the basic or central nature of something.

records.definition: 在没有确证时推想、怀疑某事可能属实；作者由研究产生了对制宪者真实意图的怀疑。
records.otherSenses:
1) 怀疑某人犯了错或犯罪：suspect sb of sth/doing sth
2) 觉得某事不完全可靠、合法或诚实
3) suspect（名词）：嫌疑人
4) suspect（形容词）：可疑的；不可信的
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
suspect that ... 认为……很可能
suspect sb of doing sth 怀疑某人做了某事
suspect foul play 怀疑有人作恶
I suspect so/not. 我想是／不是。

Contrast:
suspect：倾向于认为是真的，但尚未证实
doubt：倾向于不相信是真的
assume：暂时把某事当作已知前提
infer：根据线索作出推断

Word Family / Formation:
suspect v. / n. 怀疑；嫌疑人
suspicion n. 怀疑；猜疑
suspicious adj. 怀疑的；可疑的
suspiciously adv. 怀疑地；可疑地

Usage Note:
动词重音在后：/səˈspekt/；名词“嫌疑人”重音在前：/ˈsʌspekt/。
I suspect that he is right = 我觉得他很可能是对的；I doubt that he is right = 我不太相信他是对的。
本文是研究后形成的猜想，不应在译文或改写中把制宪者的意图写成已证实的事实。
records.examples: suspect: People already suspect this is a recovery for the rich and ongoing recession for the rest. [https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2013/sep/24/ed-miliband-labour-conference-speech-verdict]
records.definitionEn: To think that something is probably true without having definite proof; the writer's research led him to doubt the constitution-makers' real intentions.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) suspect somebody of something/doing something: to believe that someone may have done something wrong or illegal.
2) To think that something may not be reliable, legal or honest.
3) suspect (noun): a person believed to have committed a crime.
4) suspect (adjective): possibly false, dangerous or untrustworthy.

records.definition: 被视为至高、不可质疑而受到崇敬的；这里的 sacred Constitution 带有对传统神圣化态度的暗示。
records.otherSenses:
1) 与神或宗教有关的；神圣的
2) 极其重要并受到高度尊重的
3) 不可改变或不可挑战的；神圣不可侵犯的
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a sacred text/site 宗教经典／圣地
a sacred duty 神圣职责
be sacred to sb 对某人而言神圣不可侵犯

Contrast:
sacred：因宗教、价值观或情感而被视为不可侵犯
holy：直接与神或宗教神圣性有关
inviolable：不可侵犯，强调规则或权利的保护
revered：备受崇敬，强调人们的态度

Word Family / Formation:
sacred adj. 神圣的；不可侵犯的

Usage Note:
本文 sacred 带修辞意味：宪法受到近乎神圣的尊崇。不要机械译为“宗教性的宪法”。
sacred 是两音节 /ˈseɪkrɪd/，结尾不是 /kt/。
records.examples: sacred: It is a sacred moment, and you feel blessed merely to have witnessed it. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2015/feb/08/poor-glasgow-safe-seat-cranhill-labour-snp-election-voters]
records.definitionEn: Regarded with such deep reverence that it should not be questioned or challenged; sacred Constitution hints at a tradition of treating the document as untouchable.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Connected with God, a god or religion.
2) Considered extremely important and deserving great respect.
3) Treated as inviolable, so that it must not be changed or challenged.

records.definition: 民主的；由人民选出的代表治理、体现人民政治权利的。
records.otherSenses:
1) 组织内部成员有平等参与管理权的
2) 强调社会成员平等、不按财富或阶级划分的
3) Democratic：美国民主党的
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
democratic government 民主政府
democratic process 民主程序
democratic election 民主选举

Contrast:
democratic：决策权来自人民或成员的平等参与
representative：由代表行使权力，强调参与方式
constitutional：受宪法规则约束，不能据此直接推定民主程度
authoritarian：权力集中、限制服从者参与和异议

Word Family / Formation:
democracy n. 民主；民主制度
democrat n. 民主主义者
democratic adj. 民主的
undemocratic adj. 不民主的
democratically adv. 以民主方式

Usage Note:
democratic 是形容词；democracy 是民主制度。Democrat 大写时可指美国民主党成员，小写 democrat 指民主主义者；Republican 大写时可指美国共和党成员，小写 republican 通常指拥护共和制的。
美国两党名称是专有名词，首字母大写：the Democratic Party / the Republican Party。它们不能替代 democratic / republican 这两个普通形容词的语法和词义判断。
本文 a democratic government 的性质是作者提出的问题，不要把所有 constitutional government 自动等同于 democratic government。
records.examples: democratic: In the post-war period the Fabian Society was at the heart of Labour and social democratic thinking. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2001/aug/13/thinktanks.uk]
records.definitionEn: Based on government by elected representatives and on the political rights of the people.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Giving members of an organization equal rights to take part in its management or decisions.
2) Treating people as equals rather than according to wealth or social class.
3) Democratic: connected with the Democratic Party in the United States.

records.definition: 拿破仑·波拿巴；原句说作者童年时会在想象游戏中把自己当作拿破仑。
records.otherSenses:
1) napoleon（小写名词，北美用法）：一种分层酥皮甜点
2) napoleon（小写名词，历史用法）：以拿破仑命名的法国金币
3) Napoleonic（形容词）：拿破仑的；拿破仑时代的
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
Napoleon Bonaparte 拿破仑·波拿巴
the Napoleonic Wars 拿破仑战争
Napoleonic France 拿破仑时期的法国
pretend/play that one is Napoleon 假扮拿破仑

Contrast:
Napoleon：人物专名，指法国军事与政治领袖拿破仑·波拿巴
Napoleonic：形容词，表示“拿破仑的；拿破仑时代的”
Napoleon complex：非正式说法，指用强势行为弥补自卑；不宜当作正式心理学诊断

Usage Note:
本文 play I was Napoleon 是旧式叙述用法，接近 pretend that I was Napoleon。Napoleon 是专有名词，首字母必须大写。
records.examples: Napoleon: The Duke was given a state funeral after defeating Napoleon at Waterloo in 1815. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/w3cswsjm]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: the Napoleonic Wars（Oxford Learner’s 无 Napoleon 独立人物词条，链接包含人物说明的文化条目）
records.definitionEn: Napoleon Bonaparte, the French military leader and emperor; as a child, the writer imagined himself playing Napoleon.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) napoleon (North American English): a layered pastry dessert.
2) napoleon (historical): a French gold coin named after Napoleon.
3) Napoleonic (adjective): relating to Napoleon or his period.

records.definition: 设陷阱捕猎动物的人，尤指为获取毛皮而捕猎者；原句是作者童年想象扮演的角色。
records.otherSenses:
1) 泛指使用陷阱捕捉动物的人
2) fur trapper：以获取毛皮为目的的捕猎者；这是该词最常见的具体用法
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
fur trapper 毛皮猎人
a trapper's cabin 捕兽人的小屋

Contrast:
trapper：以陷阱捕捉动物的人
hunter：泛指猎人

Word Family / Formation:
trap n. / v. 陷阱；设陷阱捕捉
trapper n. 捕兽者
trapped adj. 被困住的

Usage Note:
trapper 指用陷阱捕猎的人；本文与 Napoleon 并列，都是童年幻想扮演的角色。
trap 加后缀要双写 p：trapped、trapping、trapper；复数 trappers。
records.examples: trapper: The last major atrocity was triggered by a fight about an indigenous woman that lead to a white dingo trapper being murdered. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2010/oct/03/alice-spring-murder-racism]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: trapper（该词通常只有这一核心义）
records.definitionEn: A person who catches animals in traps, especially for their fur; in the source sentence, it is one of the roles the writer imagined playing as a child.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) More generally, anyone who catches animals by using traps.
2) fur trapper: a person who traps animals specifically for their fur, the word's most common specific use.

records.definition: 制作、形成的过程；the making of the American Constitution 指美国宪法的制定过程。
records.otherSenses:
1) be the making of sb：使某人成长、成功或变得更好
2) have the makings of sth：具备成为某事物所需的素质
3) in the making：正在形成或制作中
4) of your own making：由自己造成的
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
the making of a film 电影制作过程
the making of a constitution 宪法制定过程
in the making 在形成中

Contrast:
the making of：着重从无到有的过程
creation：强调创造行为或成果
formation：强调逐步形成组织、结构或特征
drafting：指起草文本，是宪法制定过程的一部分

Word Family / Formation:
make v. 制作；使形成
made v. make 的过去式和过去分词
maker n. 制造者
making n. 制作；形成

Usage Note:
这里 making 有 the 限定，并用 of 引出对象，是表示过程的名词化形式；不是进行时。
the making of a film 是拍摄／制作过程；be the making of sb 则指使某人成功的重要因素。
records.examples: making:Controversy was the making of the prize. [https://www.newyorker.com/?p=1969901]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: making（Excel 的 makings 与原句不符，已按原句校正；复数保留在 term 中便于匹配）
records.definitionEn: The process of creating or forming something; the making of the American Constitution means the process by which the Constitution was produced.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) be the making of somebody: to make someone successful or help them develop into a better person.
2) have the makings of something: to have the qualities needed to become something.
3) in the making: in the process of being formed or produced.
4) of your own making: caused by your own actions.

records.definition: 具有特定特点或事件的一段历史时期；原句泛指各个时代。
records.otherSenses:
1) 新时代或阶段，如 a new era of peace
2) （地质学）代；宙之下的时间划分
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a new era 新时代
the modern era 现代
an era of change 变革时代
the Common Era 公元（CE）

Contrast:
era：以鲜明事件或特征界定的时期
period：一段时间，最中性
age：较长的历史阶段，也可指人的年龄
epoch：划时代的时期，学术或正式语境较常见

Usage Note:
era 是可数名词，复数为 eras。本文 other events, men, and eras 是并列宾语，后面的 waiting for students 是现在分词短语，修饰三者。
records.examples: era: The era when Nigeria's rulers could take the people for granted is no more. [https://www.theguardian.com/global/commentisfree/2015/mar/31/nigeria-election-muhammadu-buhari-revolution-voted-change]
records.definitionEn: A period of history marked by particular events or characteristics; in the source sentence, it refers generally to different historical periods.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) A new period or stage, as in a new era of peace.
2) In geology, a major division of time below an eon.

records.definition: 彼此说法不一致的；disagreeing authorities 指对历史事实或解释持不同意见的权威资料或学者。
records.otherSenses:
1) disagree with sb about/on/over sth：与某人在某事上意见不同
2) disagree with a statement/view：不赞同某种说法或观点
3) （报告、数字等）互不一致、给出不同信息
4) disagree with sb：食物等使某人身体不适
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
disagree with sb 不同意某人
disagree about/on/over sth 对某事意见不一
strongly/fundamentally disagree 强烈／根本不同意
disagreeing accounts 相互矛盾的说法

Contrast:
disagree：人与人意见不同；也可指说法彼此不一致
differ：更中性，表示观点、性质或事实存在差异
object：明确表示反对某个提议或做法
dispute：质疑某个说法的真实性或正确性

Usage Note:
本文 disagreeing authorities 指“观点相互冲突的权威作者”。谈论意见时通常说 disagree with somebody、disagree about/on something。
records.examples: disagreeing: The talks are progressing slowly, with countries still disagreeing over issues such as finance from developed to poor countries, helping them cut emissions and adapt to climate change, and the wording of the final text. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2012/dec/06/doha-conference-black-carbon-methane]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: disagree（disagreeing 无独立页，链接动词父词条）
records.definitionEn: Holding different opinions or giving conflicting accounts; disagreeing authorities are experts or sources that do not agree about historical facts or their interpretation.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) disagree with somebody about/on/over something: to have a different opinion from someone on an issue.
2) disagree with a statement/view: not to accept an idea or claim as correct.
3) Of reports, figures or accounts: to be inconsistent and provide different information.
4) disagree with somebody: of food, weather or a condition, to make someone feel ill.

records.partOfSpeech: 现在分词作形容词（clinch v.）
records.definition: 起决定作用的；能最终证实结论的。clinching evidence 指足以定论的确凿证据。
records.otherSenses:
1) clinch a victory/deal：最终赢得胜利或谈成交易
2) clinch an argument：使论证获得决定性优势
3) clinch the matter/it：把尚未确定的事情最终敲定
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
clinching evidence 决定性证据
clinch a deal 敲定交易
clinch a victory/title 锁定胜利／冠军

Contrast:
clinching：足以使争论或决定最终落定
conclusive：证据能确定地支持结论，学术表达常用
convincing：令人信服，但未必排除所有其他可能

Word Family / Formation:
clinch v. 敲定；赢得；使成定局
clinching adj. 决定性的；足以定论的

Usage Note:
clinching 在本文修饰 evidence，表示足以定论。词典中的 clinch 读 /klɪntʃ/，加 -ing 后读 /ˈklɪntʃɪŋ/。
clinch 常见于新闻和非正式表达，不能把它笼统标成正式词；较正式论证可用 conclusive evidence。
不要与 cinch“轻而易举的事／束紧”混淆。
records.examples: cliching: It is odd that this was regarded as a clinching argument, as there are more than enough jets in Afghanistan. [https://www.economist.com/britain/2010/11/11/the-seat-of-their-pants]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: clinch (verb)（clinching 作为派生形式列在父词条）
records.definitionEn: Decisive and sufficient to settle a question; clinching evidence is proof strong enough to establish a conclusion finally.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) clinch a victory/deal: to finally secure a win or successfully complete an agreement.
2) clinch an argument: to give an argument a decisive advantage.
3) clinch the matter/it: to settle something that was still uncertain.

records.definition: 虚荣心；对自己的外表、能力或成就过度自负。
records.otherSenses:
1) （文学用法）空虚、无价值或无足轻重
2) vanities（复数）：表现虚荣的行为或态度
3) （北美英语）带镜子和抽屉的梳妆台
4) （北美英语）装有洗手盆和下方柜体的浴室柜
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
personal vanity 个人虚荣
appeal to sb's vanity 满足某人的虚荣
vanity about sth 对……的虚荣

Contrast:
vanity：在意别人羡慕自己，常涉及外表或成就
pride：因成就或归属而自豪，也可能过度
conceit：过高评价自身能力或重要性
self-esteem：对自身价值的基本认同，不等于虚荣

Word Family / Formation:
vanity n. 虚荣；自负
vain adj. 虚荣的；徒劳的
vainly adv. 徒劳地；虚荣地

Usage Note:
vanity 在本文是不可数抽象名词；then 限定当时的主要动机，并非宣称作者从不虚荣。
vainly 通常表示“徒劳地”，不应机械地一律翻成“虚荣地”；in vain = 徒劳。
records.examples: vanity: He was no stranger to vanity, and would make good use of his appearance. https://www.economist.com/baobab/2013/12/05/the-long-walk-is-over[]
records.definitionEn: Excessive pride in one's appearance, abilities or achievements.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) In literary use, the quality of being empty, worthless or unimportant.
2) vanities: actions or attitudes that display excessive pride.
3) In North American English, a dressing table with a mirror and drawers.
4) In North American English, a bathroom unit consisting of a washbasin set into a cabinet.

records.partOfSpeech: 现在分词作形容词（rule v.）
records.definition: 占支配地位的；主导的。ruling passion 指最强烈、最能支配一个人的欲望或激情。
records.otherSenses:
1) ruling party/class：执政的；统治的
2) ruling（名词）：有权者作出的正式决定，尤指法院裁决
3) rule a country/group：统治国家或群体
4) rule on a case：就案件作出正式裁定
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a ruling passion 主导性的热情
a passion for history 对历史的热爱
be driven by curiosity 受好奇心驱动

Contrast:
ruling passion：最能左右一个人的强烈兴趣或欲望，较书面
main concern：主要关心的问题，不一定带热情
motivation：促使行动的动机，可有多个

Word Family / Formation:
rule v. / n. 统治；支配；规则
ruler n. 统治者；尺子
ruling adj. / n. 主导的；裁决
passion n. 强烈感情；热情

Usage Note:
ruling 修饰 passion，不是现在进行时，也不指某个统治者。
本文 my ruling passion 是整句表语；语境所强调的驱动力是求知，而非虚荣。
records.examples: ruling: The opposition said it was a device to help the ruling party. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2015/mar/10/foreign-troops-retake-nigerian-towns-from-boko-haram]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: rule (verb)（原句“支配、主导”义来自父词条；ruling 形容词独立页主要指“统治的”）
records.definitionEn: Having the strongest influence or control; a ruling passion is the most powerful desire or emotion governing a person.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) ruling party/class: the party or social group that governs.
2) ruling (noun): an official decision, especially one made by a court.
3) rule a country/group: to govern or control it.
4) rule on a case: to make an official decision about it.

records.partOfSpeech: 现在分词作形容词（quicken v.）
records.definition: 正在增强、变得活跃的；a quickening sense 指逐渐强烈起来的意识。
records.otherSenses:
1) 使速度加快或自身变快，如 quicken one’s pace
2) 使兴趣、活动或反应更活跃、更强烈
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a quickening sense of purpose 逐渐增强的目标感
quicken interest 激发兴趣
quicken the pace 加快节奏
one’s pulse quickens 脉搏加快

Contrast:
quickening：感觉变得更活跃、更强烈，较书面
growing：逐渐增强或增多，中性
awakening：原来未意识到，现在开始觉醒
accelerating：速度变快，不适合直接解释本文 sense

Word Family / Formation:
quick adj. 快的
quicken v. 加快；使活跃
quickening adj. 逐渐增强或活跃的
quickly adv. 迅速地

Usage Note:
quickening 在本文是现在分词作定语，sense 是中心名词。定义应写“逐渐增强的”，不能把 quickening 本身定义成“一种感觉”。
a sense that ... 后接内容从句；本文两个 that 从句都说明 sense 的内容。
原文较书面，现代转述可用 a growing awareness。
records.examples: quickening: The aims of some state experiments now under way include the revitalization of intermediary institutions between individuals and government, and a quickening sense of urban community. [https://www.nytimes.com/1998/05/24/books/kennedy-family-values.html]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: quicken（quickening 无独立页，链接动词父词条）
records.definitionEn: Becoming stronger or more active; a quickening sense is an awareness that is gradually intensifying.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) To make something move faster or to become faster, as in quicken one's pace.
2) To make interest, activity or a reaction more lively or intense.

records.definition: 迫切需要；明显要求。is crying out to be rewritten 表示每一章历史都迫切需要重写。
records.otherSenses:
1) 因疼痛、恐惧或惊讶而大叫
2) 大声喊出某句话或名字
3) cry out for sth：迫切需要某物
4) cry out in pain/fear/alarm：因疼痛、恐惧或惊慌叫出声
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
cry out in pain/fear 痛苦／恐惧地喊叫
cry out for sth 迫切需要某事
cry out to be done 明显需要被做
cry out against injustice 大声反对不公

Contrast:
cry out：因强烈情绪喊出；也可比喻“迫切需要”
shout：泛指大声说话或喊叫
exclaim：因惊讶、激动等突然说出，常用于书面叙述
call for：要求或需要某事，语气通常没有 cry out for 强烈

Usage Note:
本文 crying out to be rewritten 是拟人化表达，意思是这些历史章节“明显而迫切地需要重写”，并非真的发出声音。
records.examples: cry out: This would obviously cry out for feminist intervention. [https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2015/entries/feminism-trans/]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: cry out for（原句用 cry out to be done；Oxford 的对应“迫切需要”义单列于此短语词条）
records.definitionEn: To be in obvious and urgent need of something; is crying out to be rewritten means that every chapter of history urgently needs rewriting.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) To shout because of pain, fear or surprise.
2) To shout particular words or a person's name loudly.
3) cry out for something: to need something urgently and obviously.
4) cry out in pain/fear/alarm: to give a sudden shout because of a strong feeling.
